human_summary: The material is a medium-length (~1000 words) section from the ACR BI-RADS® Mammography v2025 Manual, covering the BI-RADS mammography lexicon (Table 1) and an in-depth explanation of breast density categories (Table 2), including clinical significance, reporting requirements, and illustrated examples (Figures 1-16). Key takeaways for an instructor: the text defines a strict standardized terminology for mammographic findings (masses, calcifications, etc.) and a 4-category system for breast density, emphasizing its dual role in masking cancer and as a risk factor. Numerous example images demonstrate the visual appearance of each density category.

educational_units.title: BI-RADS Mammography Lexicon Terms
educational_units.description: The standardized set of terms for describing mammographic findings, including mass characteristics (shape, margin, density), calcification types (benign, suspicious morphology, distribution), architectural distortion, asymmetries, lymph nodes, skin lesions, etc.

educational_units.title: Breast Density Categories (BI-RADS A-D)
educational_units.description: The four categories of breast composition (A: almost entirely fatty, B: scattered areas, C: heterogeneously dense, D: extremely dense) based on the potential to obscure cancer, not just percentage of tissue.
educational_units.evidence: Table 2 and text describing the 2025 classification change from percentage to masking likelihood.

educational_units.title: Clinical Significance of Breast Density
educational_units.description: Dense breasts reduce mammographic sensitivity (masking effect) and are an independent risk factor for breast cancer, with quantified odds ratios for categories C and D.
educational_units.evidence: Text sections 'Breast density is significant for two reasons' and the odds ratio data [12].

educational_units.title: Visual Recognition of Density Categories
educational_units.description: The ability to visually identify and assign a BI-RADS density category (A-D) to a mammogram image (DM or SM view), understanding the masking principle for category C.
educational_units.evidence: Figures 1-16 showing example images for each category with captions.

educational_units.title: Reporting and Regulatory Requirements
educational_units.description: Reporting breast density is FDA-mandated since Sept 2024; specific language must be used in reports to referring physicians and patients; singular phrasing is allowed for unilateral mammograms as of July 2025.
educational_units.evidence: Text mentioning FDA legislation, federal guidance, and the July 2025 alternative standard.

not_recommended.reason: Material contains 16 example mammography images (Figures 1-16) perfect for visual recognition, but CLICK tasks require manual image authoring in the editor and cannot be auto-generated from this text.
Similarly, DRAW tasks for outlining density regions would be highly relevant but require manual creation with the provided example images as base.
Illustrations are present. Image-based tasks are not auto-generated in this flow; consider manually creating 2-4 image tasks in the editor for visual recognition/classification.

illustrations_note: The material includes 16 labeled figures (Figures 1-16) showing example mammograms (DM and SM views) for each BI-RADS density category (A-D). These are ideal for creating CLICK (find/label) or DRAW (outline) tasks to assess visual recognition of density patterns and the masking effect principle. However, such tasks must be created manually in the editor using these images.

body.text: This material contains 16 illustrative mammography figures (DM/SM views) for density categories A-D. To assess visual recognition (Unit 4), you must manually create CLICK (point to correct category) or DRAW (outline dense areas) tasks in the editor using these images. Automated text-based generation cannot create these image-interaction tasks.
